hypothesis: Two real cases where boundary extraction needed phasing will indicate the build-trigger; skill-use log helps measure when this fires.
summary: A planning skill for staged boundary decoupling. Consumes a staging-decision-framework ADR + an /impact-feature output + a /propose-boundary artifact, then produces a phase-graph (nodes = phases, edges = predecessors) with phase-boundary verification gates and partial-revert plans. Build only after the staging-decision-framework ADR lands AND a real boundary extraction surfaces a P0 staging fork.
title: /plan-phased-refactor skill for staged decoupling

hypothesis: Coherence drift can be measured by cross-package change-amplification + cross-package import directionality + concept fingerprint overlap. Open question whether this rolls up cleanly enough to be actionable.
summary: Higher-abstraction analog to SOLID: detects when a system as a whole drifts from internal coherence. Cousin to /find-folder-topology-drift but at the system-of-subsystems level. Candidate signals: concepts fighting across modules, subsystem boundaries dissolved by features that cross them, change-amplification that crosses package walls.
title: System-coherence drift detector

summary: Backfill skill-use logging across every existing skill rather than opt-in-as-touched. Would give immediate full coverage but requires touching every skill's terminal stage. Trade-off: speed of evidence accumulation vs upfront instrumentation cost. Engineering-skills owns this question since the shared library is where skills land first.
title: Retroactive skill-use logging across existing ecosystem

hypothesis: Grouping by job (find/propose/refactor/map/decide/track/extract/etc.) will surface seams that motivate orchestration layers and reveal which large skills are split-candidates.
summary: Apply folder-organization conventions (>=3-sibling packaging threshold; see host project decision registry) to .claude/skills/. Today's catalog is flat (~30+ skills); natural groups exist (find-* / propose-* / refactor-* / map-* / decide / track-*). The conventions codified for the codebase should apply to the skill ecosystem itself.
title: Apply folder-organization rules to .claude/skills/

summary: Hash vs verbatim target paths; retention/rotation policy beyond the basic compaction-and-archive mechanism; commit-gate criteria for the active log. Defer until log size or commit pressure makes the question concrete. The compaction mechanism handles growth but not privacy.
title: Skill-use log privacy and retention policy

hypothesis: There is a missing midpoint between '/refactor-subsystem extracts N files' and 'leave it bad': a single-file reorganizer that clusters symbols by domain, adds banner comments + a top-of-file index, declares __all__, and emits no semantic changes. Many 1K-LOC omnibuses are tolerable when sensibly organized; not all need extraction.
origin: Conversation in host project 2026-05-14 on omnibus follow-up options
summary: Skill that takes an omnibus file as input and produces a structurally-reorganized version with: (1) symbol clustering by domain (reuse the same head-noun clustering /find-omnibus uses), (2) section banner comments grouping each cluster, (3) a top-of-file index/TOC docstring, (4) an explicit __all__ declaration listing the public API in order, (5) zero semantic changes. Default --require-recent-edits gate skips files with no edits in 90+ days unless --force ('leave stable files alone'). Outputs a --dry-run move plan first. Tooling caveat: a whole-file reorder buries git-blame trails — mitigated by 'git log --follow' / 'git blame -w -CC' which preserve authorship across moves; report should hint at these flags. Slots into the maintenance loop as a sibling to /refactor-subsystem: /find-omnibus → DECISION (decompose | reorganize | leave) → /refactor-subsystem OR /organize-file OR skip. Composes with: /propose-boundary (when reorg surfaces a clean seam, re-evaluate as a refactor candidate); the staged-boundary ADR (refuse-phasing rules apply if a reorg unexpectedly grows into a refactor).
title: /organize-file — reorganize an omnibus without restructuring

hypothesis: Two-token prefix or verb-stripping logic would surface the obviously-correct seams that humans see immediately. The current single-token approach is too eager to collapse.
summary: Naming clusters use first-token-after-generic-verb-strip as cluster key. e.g. 'save_html_to_file' and 'save_screenshot_to_file' both land in the 'save_*' cluster, but the real semantic cluster is 'file I/O' (which also wants 'url_to_filename'). The skill misses obvious file-I/O / crawl / discovery clusters when the head-noun is generic. Candidate fix: two-token prefix OR head-noun-after-verb extraction. Evidence: a real shared-helper file showed 3 weak prefix seams while manual reading shows >=3 strong semantic clusters.
title: /propose-boundary naming clusters are single-token-prefix only

hypothesis: Most real targets have lifetime > 90 days; the default should reflect that. A loud empty-signal warning + auto-widening would prevent silent quality degradation.
summary: Default --co-edit-days=90 returns 0 co-edit pairs for active code if all activity is older than the window (or the file was renamed and git log doesn't follow rename). Candidate seams then score co_edit_intensity=0.00; only naming signal carries. Candidate fixes: (a) default to 180+ days, (b) make window relative to file mtime, (c) warn loudly when co-edit signal is empty so the human knows naming-only scores are weaker evidence.
title: /propose-boundary co-edit signal empty when target has no recent git history

hypothesis: Every project with the Claude harness will have .claude/worktrees/ pollution. A default skip-glob is high-value, near-zero risk.
summary: Proposal for a shared helper listed ~150 importers; ~80% were duplicates from stale agent worktrees under .claude/worktrees/agent-*. These worktrees contain old copies of the codebase. Inflates importer counts, dilutes 'callers_into_private_helpers', and makes the report harder to scan. Candidate fix: ship with default --skip-path-glob '.claude/worktrees/**' (and maybe also '**/.venv/**' though Python AST should not import .venv anyway). Trivial change; broad impact.
title: /propose-boundary should default-skip .claude/worktrees/

hypothesis: find-omnibus already solved this with a JSON+md split; mirroring that pattern is the right move.
summary: --output accepts any path including X.md but writes a JSON data dump (multi-MB for nontrivial targets). Misleading filename suggests human-readable markdown. Candidate fixes: (a) rename flag to --output-json (consistent with find-omnibus's --output-md / --output-json split), (b) add a markdown renderer that consumes the JSON and produces a scannable report — same pattern as find-omnibus's report.py. (b) is the better fix because it preserves machine-readable data for downstream skills while also giving humans a readable surface.
title: /propose-boundary --output X.md writes JSON, not markdown

hypothesis: Augment the report with either (a) a verb-phrase summary per cluster ('formats *', 'sanitizes *') instead of bare nouns, or (b) a 5-line head-of-file summary the skill prompts the user to write before deciding. Either way, the cluster-name column should not be the primary disambiguator — risk score plus a one-line semantic hint should be.
summary: Top-N omnibus shortlist showed cluster names that didn't match the real concerns of the file. A high-LOC export file reported clusters as 'iter, export, notes, flatteneddata' — but the architect-skim concerns were dimension-formatting, image-sanitization, cross-DB JOIN, and downstream wiring. The detector picks the most frequent head-nouns, not the semantically distinct concerns. Result: humans have to open the file to know whether decompose vs reorganize is the right call.
title: /propose-boundary cluster names hide intent on dense files

hypothesis: Path(__file__).parent / 'literal' is a Python idiom; every Python project with refactors will eventually hit this bit-rot. The skill is one of the cheapest guardrails available.
summary: Host project shipped a /find-broken-file-refs skill (advisory SUSPECT scan for Python Path(__file__).parent / 'literal' expressions whose target doesn't exist on disk). Catches refactor-induced bit-rot in self-anchored asset paths. SKILL.md currently references Django render() in not_for; needs scrubbing for the engineering-skills mirror (Python-general, framework-agnostic). Pairs with ADR 0015 (refactor-asset-path-verification). Skill scope is universally applicable to any Python codebase with relocatable modules + literal-asset paths.
title: Mirror /find-broken-file-refs skill (host: pnci-pricing → engineering-skills)

hypothesis: Asset-path bit-rot is a universal Python refactor failure mode. A template ADR + the suspect skill together close it cheaply.
summary: Host project shipped ADR 0015: every Python file move must prove Path(__file__) constants still resolve. Decision is anchored by two real production incidents where modules moved a directory deeper and their .parent chain silently resolved to the wrong location, with the failure surfacing only at runtime. Engineering-skills mirror should be the template form (decision sections present, concrete N thresholds/incident IDs replaced with placeholders for adopters to fill in). Pairs with /find-broken-file-refs intake and /refactor-subsystem Phase 6.0.5 gate.
title: Mirror ADR 0015 (refactor-asset-path-verification) as a template

hypothesis: The 5th-tier migration was per-skill (not bulk). propose-boundary was probably migrated in engineering-skills first; the host fork needs a one-line catchup.
summary: Cross-direction sync finding: engineering-skills propose-boundary/scripts/propose.py uses the centralized _common/skill_use.py log_event helper, but host project pnci-pricing's version still has the older local _log_skill_use function. This means at least one host hasn't yet completed the skill-use 5th-tier migration. Either (a) host pnci-pricing should update propose-boundary's script to use _common/skill_use.py, or (b) engineering-skills should retain compatibility for hosts still on the pre-centralization helper. Captured here for visibility; the actual sync may be a one-line edit in the host's script.
title: Host propose-boundary script still has local skill-use logger (pre-_common migration)

hypothesis: An atlas authored once saves the manual Explore-agent passes that real-project observational synthesis tends to require. Provides L3 input surface that /propose-boundary lacks.
summary: Produces a one-page project atlas: one line per top-level subsystem with shape, dependents, dependencies, co-edit neighbors, importance-map tier. Sibling to /map-subsystem at one abstraction higher (L3 instead of L2). Output feeds /propose-boundary (with --scope=project, if added) and /propose-architecture (when that lands). Possible overlap with /propose-folder-reorganization — needs scoping pass first to clarify whether to extend that skill or build separately. Natural output home: a .claude/docs/atlas.md surface authored once + refreshed periodically.
title: /map-project skill — project-level atlas (L3 abstraction)

hypothesis: Without an authored constraints surface, any architecture-level proposal skill will hallucinate vendor-coupling, hot-path assertions, or team-ownership facts. With the surface, a small skill can produce highly contextual recommendations. Pilot: declare one entry, then validate downstream skill output reflects it.
origin: host-project conversation 2026-05-14 on constraint-aware boundary proposal
summary: Authored surface declaring architectural constraints the code alone can't reveal: (1) tight-integration zones (vendor-coupled code that shouldn't be abstracted — the file's value is co-location of vendor quirks); (2) hot paths (where network hops between modules are unacceptable); (3) failure domains (independent-failure modules, circuit-breakable); (4) team ownership (multi-team adopters). Possibly extends importance-map.md (ADR 0016) as new locator kinds, or a sibling constraints-map.md. Prerequisite for /propose-architecture — completion-trained models will fabricate these signals if not given them.
title: constraints-declaration-surface — authored inputs for constraint-aware architecture

hypothesis: The most valuable architecture insights come from the disagreement between lenses, not from either alone. A skill that surfaces disagreement is much higher-leverage than either lens alone.
origin: host-project conversation 2026-05-14 on constraint-aware boundary proposal
summary: Higher-abstraction sibling to /propose-boundary. Consumes project atlas (from /map-project) + constraints-declaration-surface, produces three-bucket output: (1) structural-clean seams to act on; (2) structural seams to leave coupled with constraint rationale (vendor-coupling, hot-path proximity, failure-domain co-location); (3) deployment-seam candidates (microservice / library / separate-repo) with constraint evidence (distinct scaling profile, independent failure domain, stable narrow contract, team alignment). Headline value: surfacing DISAGREEMENT between structural and constraint lenses (e.g. 'structural says split, constraint says encapsulate'). Output framed as evidence for a System-tier deliberation chain, not a verdict.
title: /propose-architecture skill — constraint-aware optimal-shape proposal

hypothesis: Multi-team adopters will hit Conway's-Law boundary questions immediately on adoption. An /propose-architecture run with a team-ownership map should produce visibly different recommendations than the same run without one.
origin: host-project conversation 2026-05-14 on team-organization in boundary design
summary: Explicit orthogonal-concern intake for team-ownership boundaries. Conway's Law: organizations design systems mirroring their communication structures. When multiple teams own slices of a codebase, optimal boundaries follow team lines to minimize coordination tax — sometimes overriding structural cleanliness. Inverse case (two teams stepping on one file) is a coordination-tax signal that argues for splitting even when the structural seam is messier. Critical for multi-team adopters; degenerate for single-team projects. Likely shape: a field within constraints-declaration-surface (kind=team-ownership locator + team name), not a separate file.
title: Conway's Law overlay — team-ownership boundaries as architecture force

summary: The ecosystem grew from a Django host: many lint rules, scripts, and skill calibrations carry Django/Python assumptions, so generalizing beyond Django currently falls to whoever ports it (per the existing porting contract in .claude/skills/_common/portability-roadmap.md). Ship a maintained suite of non-Django default lint rules plus skill calibrations per language — TypeScript, Rust, Go, … — each refined by dogfooding real open-source projects in that language, so the pack becomes adoptable out of the box without per-importer porting work. Explicitly backlog, not scheduled — captured as a direction, not a committed plan.
title: Non-Django default lint/skill suites per language, refined via OSS dogfooding

hypothesis: Plan/spec/SKILL.md artifacts are DAGs flattened into numbered lists; the list hides the dependency structure (permitting silent inconsistency) and the parallelism (hiding the critical path). Declaring each stage's inputs and outputs as an explicit graph yields both consistency-checking and critical-path scheduling from one representation. Open question: authoring cost, and whether the graph is hand-authored or inferred from existing stage headings.
summary: Plan, spec, and SKILL.md artifacts are dependency graphs flattened into numbered lists. The list format hides which steps actually depend on which — permitting silent inconsistency (a step consuming an input nothing upstream produced) and hiding what is parallelizable versus on the critical path. Proposal: each stage declares its inputs and outputs so the artifact carries an explicit stage-IO graph. One representation pays twice — it can be mechanically checked (the IO graph must close) and scheduled (critical path = longest dependency chain; everything off it parallelizes). Surfaced by dogfooding this ecosystem's own process: the WS1-WS4 plan run this session presented four workstreams as sequential 1-2-3-4 when WS1/WS2/WS4 were nearly independent, and stated a guessed disposition for specs.py as fact because the prose had no slot to mark that it depended on an upstream scout verdict (which later contradicted it). plan-phased-refactor-skill is the narrow instance — a phase-graph for one boundary refactor; this is the general principle under it. Feeds the instruction-artifact coherence detector: the IO-closure check is only possible once the graph is declared.
title: Dependency-explicit plan and skill artifacts — declare the stage-IO graph, not a numbered list

hypothesis: A SKILL.md / plan / spec is an executable spec written in English with no compiler or test suite to punish internal contradiction. Its coherence is checkable structurally — frontmatter vs body, stage-IO graph closure, reference resolution — with no semantic NLP. Open question: what fraction of real incoherence is structurally detectable versus needs human judgment.
summary: All nine architectural smells in the catalog target host code; none targets the ecosystem's own instruction artifacts — SKILL.md, plans, specs, ADR bodies. Yet those are executable specs written in English, with no compiler or test suite to punish internal contradiction, so they drift freely. Evidence this is a real defect class: this session's framework:django mislabels on map-subsystem and find-omnibus were exactly 'frontmatter claims X, body claims not-X' — find-omnibus's own Scope section states it does not touch Django — and nothing in the catalog would catch it (find-rule-surface-drift checks the doc table against the filesystem, find-comment-drift checks comments against code; neither checks a skill artifact against itself). Proposal: a SUSPECT detector — candidate smell 10 — checking instruction artifacts for structural coherence: frontmatter agrees with body, every stage consumes only inputs produced upstream (the stage-IO graph closes), every referenced skill/file/path resolves, claims stated as fact versus assumption are distinguished. Deliberately structural, not semantic — no NLP, no 'understand causal flow'; give prose a type-checker, not a brain. decisions.py audit/link-check — a working consistency checker for ADRs, wired into CI this session — is the proven prototype to generalize. Instruction-artifact analog of system-coherence-drift-detector (which does the same at the code level). Depends on dependency-explicit-artifacts for the stage-IO-closure check.
title: Instruction-artifact coherence detector (smell 10) — a SUSPECT pass for the ecosystem's own SKILL.md / plan / spec prose

hypothesis: Code is reconciled, not derived: the docs-to-code transform is a relation, so the graph can propagate dirtiness deterministically but cannot regenerate content. Open question — what fraction of reconciliation is safely automatable as detect-and-propose versus needs gated human acceptance.
summary: Model the project as a typed DAG so a change reveals everything it affects, including docs. Three node tiers: source (ADRs, rules, style guides, hand-written subsystem docs — authored, never regenerated); derived docs (indexes, catalogs, dashboards — pure functions of their inputs, regenerate freely, the dashboard.md regen already works this way); reconciled (code, and SKILL.md prose). Authority is one-way (docs win as intent) but generation is not — code cannot be re-rendered from docs because the docs-to-code transform is a relation not a function, and code accumulates underdetermined decisions docs never captured. The graph therefore propagates typed dirtiness, not content: changing a style guide marks dependents style-dirty but requirements-clean, scoping and cost-routing each reconciliation. Reconciliation is build-system-style invalidate-then-rebuild where rebuild is LLM-or-human judgment, not a deterministic compile. Code-to-docs is covered by decision-extraction/case-law as a promotion — lifting an implicit decision to an explicit source node, React's lift-state-up move — which keeps the graph acyclic. Passive v0 is near-term and cheap: extract edges that already exist (Python imports for code-to-code; ADR applies_to for rule-to-file, which decisions.py link-check already parses and validates) into one queryable place, mark dirty, show blast radius. The active reconciliation engine is the genuine future undertaking and is model-dependent. Feasible now only because LLM labor removes the human doc-rot failure that always killed doc-driven systems; but automatic must mean detect-and-propose, never auto-apply, since auto-applying many LLM rewrites unsupervised rebuilds the vibe-coded disaster at machine speed. Generalizes dependency-explicit-artifacts from within-artifact stage-IO to across-artifact doc-to-code dependencies.
title: Docs-to-code dependency graph — typed DAG with one-way authority and dirtiness propagation

hypothesis: The comprehension tax is dominated by cacheable components (repo-shape and file-digest), so caching the MAP artifact recovers most of it with no context-rot cost; batching only helps the fix stage, only behind characterization tests, and only within a model-dependent budget calibrated by differential testing against the separated baseline.
summary: A planner that compiles an optimal execution plan for a set of skill invocations, attacking the comprehension tax — the repeated cost of re-establishing repo and file understanding once per skill per file, which was the real time sink in this ecosystem's multi-week build. Decompose the tax into four parts: repo-shape and file-digest are cacheable (the MAP-tier artifact is the natural cache); cross-finding synthesis is currently performed by no skill (the orchestrator does it by hand); fix-context blast-radius is irreducible. Lever priority: first cache shared comprehension (MAP as a required input, not an optional doc), then parallelize detection into clean windows, and only last batch fixes — the smallest and riskiest win. Detection and fixing have opposite batching profiles: detection is independent and should be parallelized (clean context per scout, which is anti-context-rot), fixing is interacting and must share one context but only behind characterization tests, within a context-rot budget that behaves like a scheduler issue width. Tests are externalized comprehension — they let the model forget, which is what makes a fix batch fit in a window. Run regimes differ: iterative (pre-commit or PR, diff-scoped — the SUSPECT tier is not yet diff-scoped, a real gap), major (full-system analysis, MAP tier), and merge (an iterative run plus cross-branch artifact-staleness detection). The separated dev bundle is both the compiler source and the test oracle: differential-test the batched distribution bundle against it the way -O2 output is tested against -O0; the distribution bundle is compiled for a target model, since safe batch width is model-dependent and must be calibrated, not guessed. The planner also absorbs cross-finding synthesis post-run. Endorsed in conversation as a good idea.
title: Skill-execution planner — a scheduler over the skill graph that reduces the comprehension tax

hypothesis: Comprehension-tax component one — per-skill repo-shape re-derivation — dominates total run cost; an enriched ledger carrying cost fields can confirm or refute this, turning a current guess into a measurement.
summary: Today reports/_meta/effectiveness.jsonl records per-run counts only (findings_total and buckets). Enrich the schema to retain per-finding traces — code excerpt, detector output, scout rationale, and the verified label including hard negatives — plus cost fields (tokens, wall-clock, context size at decision points). One small change to an artifact that already exists, with three payoffs: it makes the comprehension tax measurable instead of anecdotal; it supplies the calibration data the skill-execution-planner needs to fit safe per-model batch budgets; and it becomes a synthetic-data corpus of verified architectural-judgment traces with hard negatives — the rare and valuable kind of training data, unlike generated code which is worthless because the internet is already saturated with it. Concrete evidence the value is currently discarded: the find-omnibus scan scan-20260516-020044 produced four training-grade hard negatives (the facets_not_domains bucket — product_topology.py and three detector files, each with a facet-vs-domain rationale explaining why it looks like an omnibus but is not), and the ledger kept only the bucket count, not the rationale. This is the smallest and most concrete of the three linked intakes and the right near-term first step.
title: Verified-judgment-trace ledger — enrich effectiveness.jsonl from a per-run tally to a per-finding corpus

hypothesis: A lightweight complexity-hotspot scan gives reviewers and refactor planners a cheap first-pass lead list without turning heuristic findings into automatic optimization work.
summary: Adds a read-only SUSPECT skill for algorithmic, ORM, and structural complexity leads. It scans Python code for nested loops, membership scans, sort-in-loop patterns, QuerySet or manager calls inside loops, and high-branch functions, then writes standard report artifacts. The useful lesson from dogfooding was that performance scanners need conservative receiver heuristics and measurement-first recommendations so they generate leads rather than confident rewrites.
title: Find complexity hotspots skill

summary: Built from a host-project request inspired by Kappaemme-git/codex-complexity-optimizer, but adapted to this ecosystem as a read-only find-* skill with frontmatter, PNCI/general reading notes, fixtures, smoke coverage, report output, and catalog/kernel registration. Dogfood on site-intelligence paths caught and fixed noisy dict.get and QuerySet-iteration false positives, added max-findings validation, and kept the final recommendation language measurement-first.
Adopted into engineering-skills-2 by adding .claude/skills/find-complexity-hotspots plus skill-catalog and quality-kernel references; validation passed with smoke, ruff, and skill_meta lint.

hypothesis: Context-composition and side-effect/blast-radius analysis are two query directions over one typed, weighted, two-speed project knowledge graph; building that graph as an always-derived first-class substrate lets the quality skills become queries instead of scanners, and lets an agent classify task triviality (= bounded blast radius) instead of defensively over-engineering.
summary: Captures where the code-quality skill ecosystem should converge: an always-current, easy-to-parse, typed-and-weighted project knowledge graph as the shared substrate. Core thesis from a design conversation. (1) The two long-standing branches are the same datastore viewed from two directions: branch 1 (reduce the exploration needed to be sure of context) is a backward-plus-neighborhood walk from a task seed; branch 2 (be sure of the magnitude of a change side-effects) is a forward walk from the same seed. One graph, two traversals. (2) Triviality classification falls out for free: trivial means bounded blast radius, so an agent cannot safely call a task trivial without branch 2 — the over-engineering failure mode (the Claude-vs-Codex meme) is the rational behavior of an agent that cannot see the boundary of its own certainty. (3) Graph design: nodes are symbols, files, models, routes, tasks, contracts, domain terms, ADRs, tests, known-issues; edges are typed and layered by automatability — static edges (calls, imports, refs) are auto-derived and genuinely always-current; dynamic/registry edges (Celery dispatch-by-name, URL conf, signals, template-context) are dynamic in general but enumerable per project and declared; semantic/contract edges (must-stay-format-equivalent, serialized-into-export) and state edges (a computation change retroactively reinterprets persisted rows, the hardest class, almost nothing catches it) must be declared and accreted on surprise. (4) The honest tool output is the boundary between what the graph is sure of and what it is not, not a false-precise list of exact side-effects — and that boundary is what removes the incentive to over-engineer. (5) Two-speed freshness: always-up-to-date is honest only for the auto layer; declared layers carry per-edge provenance, confidence, and staleness markers, because a confident-looking graph that is actually guessing is worse than no graph. (6) Edges are weighted as well as typed — risk-weighting is what turns a 40-hit dump into one ranked answer, the way a senior engineer checks the 2 dangerous edges and ignores 38. (7) The reframe for the skill ecosystem: skills stop being scanners that re-derive structure and emit stale reports, and become queries and interpreters over the graph — MAP is a rendered view, SUSPECT is a graph predicate, EXPLAIN renders subgraph-plus-semantics, REFACTOR is a graph diff, GUARD is a graph invariant. Five verbs, one substrate. (8) Anti-rot discipline: derive what you can so it cannot drift from code; co-locate the declared edges next to the code they describe (a contract annotation by the function) rather than centralizing them into a new rot magnet. (9) Easy-to-parse is load-bearing, not cosmetic: a boring universal queryable format makes the graph infrastructure (PR review becomes a before/after graph diff, onboarding and the subsystem atlas become renders, health metrics become queries); a bespoke store makes it a silo. (10) Migration trigger from the current markdown-shard era (ADRs, precedents.yml, known-issues.md, find-* reports, CONTEXT.md, importance-map.md — the correct early prototype): migrate to a real store when agents start failing to join across the shards, i.e. when manual cross-referencing cost exceeds the cost of paying for the store once. Closely related to docs-to-code-dependency-graph (the docs-to-code slice of the same graph, with dirtiness propagation) and skill-execution-planner (the graph is the comprehension-tax cache that planner needs).
title: Code knowledge graph as the convergence substrate for the quality skills

hypothesis: Making the target architecture an explicit, drift-checkable artifact lets the existing incremental tiers be aimed: re-architecting becomes accumulable rather than one high-risk transform, and behavior-preserving refactors stop polishing a system inside an expired frame.
summary: The ecosystem has durable artifacts for point decisions (ADRs), for features (specs), and for CURRENT state (map-subsystem, the map-project atlas, importance-map) — but nothing holds DESIRED whole-system state. The target architecture lives only in a human head, which is why behavior-preserving refactors can only rearrange furniture inside the founding frame and can never aim at a better one (the conversation phrase: software does not rot, it outlives its founding frame). Proposal: a standing, durable target-architecture artifact (Shape B) — a sibling to the current-state atlas — plus a drift metric defined as diff(current atlas, Shape B), computable as a query once the knowledge-graph index exists. Effect: re-architecting stops being a single high-risk transform and becomes a direction that many safe small moves (the refactor tier, the System-tier chain, /decide) accumulate toward, each scored by whether it reduces drift. Distinct from propose-architecture-skill, which generates a one-shot proposal — this idea PERSISTS the chosen target and measures distance to it continuously, and propose-architecture output is the natural seed for authoring the artifact. Distinct from system-coherence-drift-detector, which measures intrinsic coherence rather than distance from a declared target. Distinct from map-project, which captures current state only. Scoped but parked: worth exploring, no build slot yet; the index keystone (code-knowledge-graph-substrate) should land first.
title: Target-architecture artifact — persist desired Shape B plus a drift metric the incremental tiers aim at

summary: Sequencing note from a design conversation (host project pnci-pricing). Of the convergence ideas, the derived knowledge-graph index is the keystone and should be built first, deliberately conservatively: keep the markdown/JSONL/YAML shards (ADRs, precedents.yml, known-issues, find-* reports, CONTEXT.md, importance-map, the idea ledger) as the git-diffable human-readable source of truth, and add the index only as a disposable derived cache rebuilt from those shards. SQLite with recursive CTEs is almost certainly enough for the dependency-graph traversals — a bespoke graph DB is not warranted yet and would trade away the shard-level diffability that is the ecosystem ethos. Keystone argument: churn detection, per-idea coverage audits, and target-architecture drift measurement each otherwise re-derive the same cross-shard joins by hand on every run, so one index pays for itself across all three. New framing the conversation added: even with flat files retained, specialized query and update tooling over them is itself the deliverable — the mental transform of a shard into a usable frame is a comprehension tax, and that tax is a direct cause of AI-agent failure, disproportionately so in high-velocity vibe coding where no human rechecks the details, so the index is a correctness and safety surface, not merely a speed optimization. Broader intent: candidate to productize for people doing too much vibe coding; the index is the load-bearing piece of any such product and will need real optimization work. Pairs with the new target-architecture-artifact intake — drift is a query over this index.

Back-link to target-architecture-artifact (the drift-metric idea is a query over this index). Reverse of the edge recorded on that intake; the earlier dev-note event passed --edges-added but the dev-note kind does not apply edges, so this edge event records it properly.

Addendum — the authority-gradient framing. docs-to-code is the ideal case not because traversal is one-way (side-effect analysis always needs both directions plus sibling expansion) but because every edge carries a designated authority side: the doc declares intent, the code conforms. That single property buys monotone one-way dirtiness propagation, near-statically-declared edges, and — the crux — findings that are actionable rather than merely alarming. An edge with an authority label yields an answer (code B violated contract C); an edge without one yields only a question (A and B diverged — which is wrong?). The dangerous edges in the general code graph (format-equivalent peer writers, ordering assumptions) are dangerous precisely because they are directionless: no designated authority. Key reframe: the messy code graph is not a different graph from docs-to-code — it is the same graph before its implicit peer-couplings have been promoted to authored contracts. Contract extraction (what the refactor skills already do) is exactly the operation that converts one undirected high-risk edge into two clean docs-to-code edges, by introducing an authority node both sides derive from. So docs-to-code-dependency-graph is not a sibling idea but a BAND of this substrate — the subset of edges that already have a clean authority gradient; the substrate is the whole graph including the not-yet-authoritative edges. This yields a concrete architectural health metric instead of a vibe: the fraction of risky coupling that has a designated authority. A codebase where every dangerous edge is authority-labelled has cheap freshness and answerable side-effects; one full of directionless peer edges makes every change a guess (the over-engineering failure mode, structurally). The graph measures that fraction; the maintenance loop's job is to raise it — push high-risk coupling from the undirected end toward the directed-authoritative end. Implication for reconciling the two ledger entries: treat docs-to-code-dependency-graph as the directed-authoritative band of code-knowledge-graph-substrate, not a separate artifact.

hypothesis: Dismissals fingerprinted on the offending code region (normalized AST node plus the evidence set the finding cited) expire on code-region change rather than elapsed time, so a finding only re-surfaces when the structure it accused has actually moved. Open questions: (a) what AST normalization level keeps re-surface rate near zero on reformat/rename while still catching real edits; (b) whether the evidence-set hash should be conjunctive (finding re-surfaces when any cited input changes) or disjunctive (only when the AST node changes); (c) how to handle scattered-concept findings that have no single node — likely fingerprint the union of cited sites, re-surface on any union member changing.
summary: Without a dismissal-memory layer, every SUSPECT skill (find-omnibus, find-implicit-state, find-complexity-hotspots, the proposed find-scattered-concept, etc.) re-emits the same known-fine findings on every run — turning the scanner from a signal into noise the moment the project has any non-trivial accumulated review history. The dismissal layer needs three properties to be useful: (1) persistence per finding-identity, not per scan; (2) selective re-surface when the underlying code-region changes, not when the calendar advances — directly analogous to the stale-detection principle in pnci-pricing (stale = no progress increment, not elapsed time); (3) survives reformat, rename, and movement that don't change semantics. The hard sub-problem is fingerprint granularity. Too coarse (file path + finding-type) re-surfaces on any unrelated edit to the file, defeating the dismissal. Too fine (exact line range + character offsets) re-surfaces on a single space change. Plausible right grain: a tuple of (finding-type, normalized-AST-node-hash for the offending node, content-hash of the evidence set the finding cited) — so a dismissal survives unrelated edits but invalidates when the accused structure or its supporting evidence changes. Mechanics: the ledger lives under .claude/quality/dismissals.jsonl (sibling to findings.jsonl in pnci-pricing), keyed by fingerprint, with reviewer, rationale, and the original finding payload preserved for audit. SUSPECT skills query the ledger after producing findings and filter dismissed entries from the user-facing report while surfacing a count and a 'show suppressed' flag. Dismissal is a first-class GUARD output — the human review step of any SUSPECT report. Open design choices to investigate during build: rationale taxonomy (false-positive / accepted-debt / intentional-deviation / superseded), expiry escape valves (force re-review after N months for accepted-debt vs never for intentional-deviation), and whether dismissals propagate across forks/branches via git or stay per-checkout. Composes with every find-* SUSPECT skill in the ecosystem; once the code-knowledge-graph substrate exists, the AST-node-hash component should be derived from the graph rather than recomputed per skill. Surfaced during pnci-pricing maintainability experiments session (2026-05-19) as the missing piece that lets SUSPECT skills graduate from one-shot scans to standing fitness functions.
title: Code-region-fingerprinted dismissal ledger for SUSPECT skills

summary:
Full substrate design captured during pnci-pricing maintainability-experiments arc (2026-05-19), preserved here before pivoting to a lean cut that defers most of this build.

Schema (10 node tables): files, symbols, models, routes, tasks, contracts, domain_terms, adrs, tests, lint_rules. Two-speed freshness: last_seen_at always-updated by importers; last_verified_at only on declared/contract layers, hand-bumped on review.

Edge taxonomy (18 edges across 4 authority layers):
- Layer 1 (static auto-derived, freshness honest): imports, calls, model_fk, model_inheritance, type_annotation_uses.
- Layer 2 (dynamic registry, per-project enumerable): celery_dispatch_by_name, url_resolves, signal_send, signal_receive, template_context_provides, template_context_uses.
- Layer 3 (test linkage, auto-derivable from coverage): test_covers, test_setup_uses.
- Layer 4 (declared semantic/contract/state, accreted on surprise): must_stay_format_equivalent, serialized_into_export, retroactively_reinterprets_persisted, contract_exports, contract_requires.

The authority-gradient framing carries through: every Layer-4 edge has a designated authority side (the contract declares intent, code conforms). Layer-1 edges are directionless but auto-fresh. The maintenance loop's job is to push high-risk Layer-1 couplings into Layer-4 by extracting contracts — converting one undirected edge into two clean authority-labelled edges.

AST normalization v1 (aggressive) for symbol-level fingerprints used by the dismissal layer and by node-identity in the graph: strip local + parameter names to LOCAL_n / PARAM_n with stable ordering; keep module-level names, call targets, string literals, decorators, attribute-access chains, and type annotations; drop docstrings, comments, whitespace; SHA256 the canonicalised AST text and truncate to the first 16 hex chars. Calibration target ≥80% correlation against human-labelled semantic-vs-cosmetic on 20 historical commits.

Build phases as originally planned (5 weeks @ ~15h/week, ~3000 LOC):
- Phase 1 (inventories — DONE under .claude/tasks/maintainability-experiments/07 and 08; the planned 09 engineering-skills-2-overlap was rolled into the lean-cut plan directly).
- Phase 2: SQLite store, 14 importers (one per node table plus key edge classes), recursive-CTE traversal predicates, health metric (fraction of risky coupling with designated authority).
- Phase 3: per-subsystem contract YAMLs (see new subsystem-contract-artifact intake), 5 pilot contracts, conscious-change loop (contract bump → dependents review-due via cross-shard query), lint-integration via enforced_by: lint:<rule>.
- Phase 4: scanner-to-query rewrites for /find-dormant, /map-subsystem, /architecture-fit; reports/_meta/graph-dashboard.md; graph.py query --format dot visualisation.

4-lane validation strategy: Lane A real-traffic dogfood (≥5 dismissals across SUSPECT skills, FP resurface rate ≤10%); Lane B backtest harness (100-commit replay, contract injection, noqa-stratified ground truth); Lane C AST-normalisation calibration (semantic-vs-cosmetic correlation on 20 historical commits); Lane D scanner-vs-substrate parity (rewritten scanners must produce supersets of the markdown-shard outputs, not different sets).

Decide-gate framework: explicit kill/adapt/keep criteria at each phase exit. Kill triggers retire the deferred intakes with retrospective notes; adapt keeps the substrate but rescopes (e.g. drop dynamic-registry layer 2 if importer cost exceeds payoff); keep is the only state that unlocks the next phase.

Lean-cut decision (2026-05-19): user chose Option B (full substrate) primarily out of loss aversion — not wanting deferred pieces to get forgotten. The engineering-skills-2 ledger is the recoverable place to park those pieces, so the right plan was a ~1.5-week three-track cut: AST-fingerprinted dismissal ledger (Track 1, in-flight under false-positive-dismissal-ledger), concept-glossary + drift audit (Track 2, addresses the _field_guidance divergence failure mode without the full substrate), consolidated findings-and-dispositions report (Track 3). See feedback-loss-aversion-in-option-selection memory for the pattern.

Revisit-when triggers for promoting this substrate back to in-flight: (a) 3+ SUSPECT skills independently need cross-cutting queries the markdown shards can't answer; (b) concept-drift audit (Track 2 lean-cut deliverable) hits >3 cases/quarter that lints don't catch; (c) the directed-authoritative band (docs-to-code-dependency-graph) is built first and proves the authority-gradient framing on a small slice.

Related intakes: docs-to-code-dependency-graph (directed-authoritative band of this same graph, lower-risk first slice), target-architecture-artifact (drift metric as a query over this index), subsystem-contract-artifact (the Layer-4 declared-edge surface), false-positive-dismissal-ledger (the dismissal layer that should consume AST-node-hash from the graph once it exists).

Greenlighted as Track 1 of the pnci-pricing maintainability lean cut (2026-05-19). Pieces being built in pnci-pricing: scripts/_lib/ast_normalize.py (~150 LOC, extends scripts/chunk_file.py's tree walker), scripts/dismissals.py CLI (~150 LOC, mirroring scripts/quality_findings.py's discipline), .claude/quality/dismissals.jsonl append-only ledger. Pilot consumer: /find-implicit-state (highest false-positive rate per inventory 08). Week-1 decide gate: ≥5 real dismissals dogfooded via CLI with rationales, FP resurface rate ≤10% on cosmetic edits, AST-normalisation calibration ≥80% correlation vs human-labelled semantic-vs-cosmetic on 20 historical commits. Graceful kill path: if calibration <80% after one tune-and-retest cycle, drop the dismissal track and salvage ast_normalize.py as a standalone library — the filter-dismissed wiring is designed to degrade to passthrough when ledger is missing or malformed, so the kill is reversible and non-destructive.

Implementation design for the lean-cut build of this layer.

AST normalisation v1 (aggressive): strip local + parameter names to LOCAL_n / PARAM_n with stable ordering; keep module-level names, call targets, string literals, decorators, attribute-access chains, and type annotations; drop docstrings, comments, whitespace; SHA256 the canonicalised AST text and truncate to the first 16 hex chars. This level of aggression intentionally tolerates rename inside a function (because most cosmetic edits do not change semantics) at the cost of missing rare cases where local-variable identity is load-bearing — calibration measures that tradeoff.

Record schema: a dismissal opens with record_kind: finding plus code_region containing ast_node_hash + evidence_set_hash; subsequent records mutate state via record_kind: event with event_kind in {invalidated, revalidated, withdrawn, expired, scope_changed, human_acked}. Append-only; no in-place mutation. Mirrors the event-history shape of .claude/quality/findings.jsonl in pnci-pricing.

CLI verbs (mirror scripts/quality_findings.py): add, list, withdraw, renew, validate, check, filter-dismissed. filter-dismissed is the integration point: SUSPECT-skill reports are piped through it, dismissed findings are stripped (with a count and a 'show suppressed' affordance), and the filter degrades to passthrough on missing/malformed ledger. .pre-commit-config.yaml gets an advisory dismissal-ledger-format JSONL-schema check — non-blocking, surfaces drift without failing the lane.

Adversarial-review mitigations baked into the lean cut:
- Calibration moves before authoring (Week-1 step 1). If <80% correlation after one tune cycle, the track dies cheaply.
- filter-dismissed always returns the input set when index/ledger is absent or malformed. Failures degrade to current behavior, not worse.
- Pre-commit hook is advisory only — never blocks a commit on dismissal-ledger format errors.
- Dogfood target ≥10 dismissals by end of Week 2 (Track-3 fix-now dismissals count toward the threshold), to avoid optimistic conclusions from a 5-sample base.
- Pilot choice (/find-implicit-state) was selected because it has the highest FP rate per inventory 08 — concentrates signal where validation matters most.
- Long-run: once code-knowledge-graph-substrate is built, the AST-node-hash component derives from the graph instead of being recomputed per skill, removing one duplicated implementation.

Open design choices to settle during build: rationale taxonomy (false-positive / accepted-debt / intentional-deviation / superseded); whether intentional-deviation dismissals are immortal or carry a force-review-after-N-months timer (lean-cut default: immortal, revisit on demand); whether dismissals propagate via git (lean-cut default: yes, the JSONL is checked in alongside findings.jsonl) or stay per-checkout.

hypothesis: Per-subsystem contract YAMLs declared next to the subsystem code (exports / requires / concept_refs / promises) give boundary lints an explicit, accreted authority side for what is currently implicit peer coupling — converting the directionless-peer-edges band of the code graph into the docs-to-code authority-labelled band one boundary at a time. With concept_ref pointers to a shared concepts.yaml glossary and lint-integration via enforced_by: lint:<rule>, each existing boundary lint becomes the enforcement mechanism for a contract violation rather than a free-standing rule with no anchor. A conscious-change loop (contract version bump → dependents marked review-due) replaces 'audit before merge' with 'audit before publish'. Open questions: (a) what fraction of pnci-pricing's 15+ boundary lints can be re-anchored without rewriting; (b) whether contract version bumps need semantic-vs-cosmetic distinction the way commit history does; (c) whether the conscious-change loop fires usefully without the graph substrate underneath (lean cut grep over requires: blocks vs full graph query); (d) which subsystem coupling has the highest cost and lowest current lint coverage — candidate is the export schema ↔ FlattenedData ↔ WWS Items chain (format-equivalence drift between parallel writers, smell 5 in architectural-smells.md).
summary:
Captures the deferred contract-artifact track from the pnci-pricing maintainability lean cut (2026-05-19). The lean cut ships only the companion .claude/contracts/concepts.yaml glossary plus a one-off /find-concept-divergence scanner; this intake preserves the full contract-format design for whenever the revisit-when triggers fire.

YAML schema: id, version, status, title, date, applies_to (path globs), exports, requires (each with concept_ref pointer), concept_refs (canonical glossary slugs), promises (semantic invariants beyond the type signature), provenance (which ADR / lint / canonical-patterns row this contract anchors), exceptions (path allowlist with rationale, mirroring no-retailer-references). Stored at .claude/contracts/<subsystem>.yaml — co-located near the subsystem code, not centralised into a new rot magnet (anti-rot discipline carried over from the code-knowledge-graph-substrate intake).

Companion glossary: .claude/contracts/concepts.yaml (the lean cut builds this surface now). Each entry: name, aliases, definition, superseded_by (for rename safety like retailer→site per ADR 0012). All contract concept_refs resolve into this single glossary, so renames cascade through the graph by editing one node.

Conscious-change loop: contract version bump triggers dependents review-due via a cross-shard query. Pre-substrate fallback: a grep over requires: blocks in sibling contracts. Post-substrate: a graph query over Layer-4 contract_requires edges. Either way, the contract is the authority — the lint is the enforcement mechanism, not the source of truth.

Lint integration scheme: each existing boundary lint gets enforced_by: lint:<rule> annotation inside the matching contract. The contract owns the intent; the lint owns the check. This breaks the current pattern where 15+ pnci-pricing lints are free-standing rules with no anchor a non-pnci-pricing reader can recover from.

5 pilot contract drafts (sketched during planning):
1. site-intelligence-readonly — the sidecar must not write to Django ORM. enforced_by: lint:site-intelligence-boundary. concept_refs: site-intelligence-sidecar, django-orm. exceptions: explicit write-back queue endpoints documented in site-intelligence-sidecar.md.
2. safe-dispatch — celery task dispatch must use safe_dispatch wrapper (no bare .delay across boundaries). enforced_by: lint:safe-dispatch. concept_refs: celery-wire-name, safe-dispatch-pattern.
3. core-wire-name-preservation — celery task names are wire-stable contracts; renames require versioning + rollover. enforced_by: lint:no-task-rename. concept_refs: celery-wire-name, task-identity. provenance: ADR 0007.
4. textchoices-state — string status comparisons forbidden against TextChoices fields. enforced_by: lint:stringly-status. concept_refs: textchoices-state, job-status.
5. retailer-to-site-renamed — Retailer* identifiers superseded by Site* outside the allowlist. enforced_by: lint:no-retailer-references. concept_refs: retailer (superseded_by: site). provenance: ADRs 0011, 0012, 0014. exceptions: migrations, ADRs 0007/0011/0012, tools/rename/.

6th pilot question raised by adversarial review (no lint enforcement yet): the export schema ↔ FlattenedData ↔ WWS Items chain — parallel-writer format-equivalence drift, the canonical example of smell 5 in architectural-smells.md. A contract here would be load-bearing precisely because no lint catches it today. If the contract format is going to add real value beyond re-anchoring existing lints, this is where it shows up first.

Revisit-when triggers for promotion to in-flight: (a) concept-drift audit (lean Track 2 deliverable) hits >3 cases/quarter that lints don't catch; (b) a mid-sized refactor breaks an implicit subsystem boundary twice (signal that implicit-peer coupling has become a tax); (c) code-knowledge-graph-substrate is built (contracts become real Layer-4 edges rather than YAML files with grep-based dependents).

Comparison to existing artifacts: precedents.yml is implementation case-law (exemplar-driven, recurring mechanism, scoped to one decision); subsystem contracts are subsystem-scoped boundary declarations (exports/requires-driven, scoped to one subsystem). Different unit of analysis, both layered onto the same code, both queryable by the future graph substrate. ADRs are decisions at a point in time; contracts are durable subsystem-interface declarations that ADRs anchor into. CONTEXT.md Language section is the human-readable mirror of concepts.yaml (the lean cut adds a header pointer between them).

Migration path: (Phase A) lean cut ships concepts.yaml + find-concept-divergence scanner — done as Track 2 of the pnci-pricing lean cut. (Phase B) draft pilot 1 (site-intelligence-readonly) as a single contract file, validate the schema against one real subsystem before generalising. (Phase C) generalise to pilots 2–5 + add the bump-triggers-review loop. (Phase D) once code-knowledge-graph-substrate is built, absorb concept_refs and contract_requires as real graph edge types and retire the grep-based fallback.

Composes with code-knowledge-graph-substrate (the Layer-4 declared-edge surface that this artifact populates), false-positive-dismissal-ledger (dismissals can cite contract-id as scope rather than file:line, surviving file moves), docs-to-code-dependency-graph (this is the directed-authoritative band of the same graph, generalised from docs to subsystem contracts), system-coherence-drift-detector (drift between contract.version and the code that should conform is a concrete coherence signal).
title: Subsystem contract artifact — explicit boundary contracts with authority-gradient enforcement

summary:
Calibration experiment complete (2026-05-19). v1 aggressive normalization scored 63.6% on an 11-sample manifest (6 semantic, 5 cosmetic). All 6 semantic samples passed (TP=6, FN=0). 4 of 5 cosmetic samples failed: 3 of those failures were in-function imports being lifted to module scope, 1 was a Retailer→Site class-reference rename (ADR 0012 Phase 1).

Tuning round 1: added in-function Import / ImportFrom node stripping. The rationale is that an import line inside a function body is a way to obtain a symbol (typically deferred for cycle-breaking), not part of the function's observable behavior. The function's behavior depends on what symbols it references, not on how it imports them. visit_Import / visit_ImportFrom return None when the renamer is inside any function scope (self._stack non-empty), and the body iteration filters Nones before re-attaching to the parent.

v2 retest: 90.91% on the same manifest (10/11 match). All 6 semantic samples still pass. 4 of 5 cosmetic samples now pass. The remaining failure (identify_retailer_from_url across e79bf9c3) is the Retailer→Site class rename case: my v1 preserves module-level names, so the AST still differs even though behavior is identical. This is documented in the module header as a known v1 limitation; tuning it would require concepts.yaml integration (rewrite names via superseded_by chain before normalization), deferred to a follow-up.

Operational implication of the limitation: dismissals attached to a function whose class-references get renamed will resurface after the rename. That is arguably correct — reviewers want to re-confirm those dismissals against the new class anyway. In contrast, dismissals against functions where only local variables, docstrings, comments, or whitespace changed will stay dismissed; and dismissals against functions whose semantics changed (added branch, changed constant, modified logic, drop unused in-body import) will reflect the change.

Confidence caveat: 11-sample manifest is small. Will expand during dogfooding (Track 3 fix-now dismissals count toward the n=10 stretch goal by end of Week 2). If real-traffic dismissals show resurface rate exceeding the calibration's 9% miss rate by a large margin, revisit the normalization rules.

Files: scripts/_lib/ast_normalize.py (177 LOC including normalization rules, CLI, and known-limitation docstring), scripts/calibrate_ast_normalize.py (calibration harness), .claude/tasks/maintainability-experiments/calibration-manifest.json (11 samples with labels). Week-1 decide gate: calibration PASS — proceed with dismissals.py build.

Lean-cut maintainability validation evidence from pnci-pricing (2026-05-19): no docs-to-code graph was needed in this pass. CONTEXT.md → concepts.yaml seeding worked as a text-only manual pull (~30 min, 15 concepts); the strict-first /find-concept-divergence scan (~200 LOC) caught the drift the lean-cut targeted (field config vs extraction_code, auto-discovery in test docstring, third-extraction-path-name flagged ambiguity confirmed by runtime evidence in app/services/site_intelligence/use_cases/models.py). Bias check: the concept-grep approach is a cheap textual proxy for what the graph would provide structurally. It found 2 real drift cases beyond the seed _field_guidance, so the substrate's marginal payoff over text-grep is not yet proven. Revisit-when: text-grep starts missing real drift cases that a graph traversal would catch (concept used through a synonym chain), or a concept-rename cascade needs to walk imports/calls.

Lean-cut maintainability validation evidence from pnci-pricing (2026-05-19): no target-architecture artifact was built. The lean cut chose to track unclear-boundary spots via .claude/tasks/maintainability-experiments/10-findings-and-dispositions.md (synthesized from 5 experiments + 3 inventories + 2 new tracks). The synthesis named the same 'set of 5 contract spots' the artifact would (setup-mode dispatcher, fieldspec consolidation, apply-boundary, promotion-gate, subsystem contracts), and dispositioned each with revisit-when triggers. 1 fix-now landed, 6 log-laters route to engineering-skills-2 intakes, 5 monitors route to .claude/tasks/lessons.md. Bias check: the artifact's marginal value over a markdown synthesis + intakes is not yet proven on this project. Revisit-when: the markdown synthesis goes stale faster than intakes do, or contract divergence needs a structural diff that prose can't provide.

Lean-cut maintainability validation evidence from pnci-pricing (2026-05-19): /find-concept-divergence in pnci-pricing is a minimum-viable instance of this substrate — strict canonical-name grep, no similarity matching, output to reports/find-concept-divergence/<scan>/ with JSONL findings + markdown report. Three drift bands: avoid_term_hit, competing_term_coexistence, superseded_co_occurrence (skippable per concept via coverage_lint field). Refinements that mattered: (a) _source_files() exclusion lets a concept's own source doc (CONTEXT.md) mention the avoid terms without firing; (b) coverage_lint: lets the retailer→site rename skip superseded_co_occurrence because no-retailer-references lint already owns identifier-level enforcement; (c) word-boundary regex with case-insensitive matching keeps identifier-friendly hits. End-to-end scan went from 146 noisy hits → 12 actionable findings (Week 1) and 57 hits (Week 2 with the new workflow-overloaded entry added, mostly natural co-occurrence) after refinements. Portable to a larger drift-detector substrate; the lessons above are v1 spec.

Lean-cut maintainability validation evidence from pnci-pricing (2026-05-19): pnci-pricing maintains instruction artifacts as CLAUDE.md + .augment/rules/imported/*.md + AGENTS.md symlink with manual cross-tool sync called out in CLAUDE.md 'Keeping Docs Current'. The lean cut added one row to the CLAUDE.md Supplementary Documentation table (.claude/contracts/concepts.yaml) and mirrored to .augment/rules/imported/context.md inline. Drift between the two surfaces was minimal because the rule is explicit. Bias check: a project with 6+ agent surfaces would amortize this substrate; pnci-pricing's three-surface footprint manages with prose + the existing find-rule-surface-drift lint. Revisit-when: a 4th or 5th agent surface needs to join the mirroring chain, or sync drift becomes a recurring source of confusion.

Lean-cut maintainability validation evidence from pnci-pricing (2026-05-19): pnci-pricing's existing artifacts cover most of what this intake proposes — 18 AST lints + 11+ ADRs + canonical-patterns.md + the new concepts.yaml. The new concepts.yaml is a cross-subsystem coherence artifact (the glossary), demonstrating the YAML+scanner shape works at glossary granularity. The open question is whether the same shape scales to subsystem-level exports/requires/promises — see subsystem-contract-artifact for that next step. Composes with subsystem-contract-artifact.

Lean-cut maintainability validation evidence from pnci-pricing (2026-05-19): Track 3 of the lean cut surfaced 4 new candidate subsystem contracts via the 10-findings-and-dispositions.md synthesis — setup-mode-typed-dispatcher (#1), fieldspec-consolidation (#2), apply-boundary-named-contract (#5), promotion-gate-collapsed (#6) — each landing as its own intake (composed with this one). The shape of these candidates confirms the contract-artifact spec: each names an exports surface (typed enum, dataclass shape, or named class), a requires surface (callers / dispatchers / gates), and concept_refs (slugs into pnci-pricing's concepts.yaml). The pnci-pricing concepts.yaml is the de-facto concept_refs substrate. Revisit-when trigger from the original intake (concept-drift audit hits >3 cases/quarter, OR mid-sized refactor breaks an implicit boundary twice) — Track 2 hit 2 cross-subsystem drift cases this quarter (field config vs extraction_code; third-extraction-path-name), so the 'twice' counter would close fast if more drift surfaces before resolution lands.

Lean-cut maintainability validation evidence from pnci-pricing (2026-05-19): the lean cut shipped the AST-normalization layer (scripts/_lib/ast_normalize.py, 177 LOC, v2 at 90.91% semantic-vs-cosmetic correlation) as standalone infrastructure for the dismissal ledger. That layer is the seed for the substrate's AST-node-hash dimension if/when the substrate is built. The lean cut deliberately did NOT build the 10-table substrate; it shipped one targeted scanner (/find-concept-divergence) consuming one YAML (concepts.yaml) instead. Substrate revisit-when triggers unchanged: 3+ SUSPECT skills need cross-cutting queries OR concept-drift audit hits >3 cases/quarter that text-grep can't catch. Concrete observations for substrate design: (a) YAML+scanner+report works at glossary granularity; (b) the dismissal ledger gives every SUSPECT skill a write-back surface; (c) normalization at function granularity is sufficient for the dismissal use case, but the substrate would need finer (statement / call-site) granularity for cross-reference queries.

Track 1 of pnci-pricing lean cut complete (2026-05-19). Shipped: scripts/_lib/ast_normalize.py (177 LOC, v2 normalization at 90.91% calibration on 11 samples), scripts/dismissals.py CLI (add/list/withdraw/renew/validate/check/filter-dismissed), .claude/quality/dismissals.jsonl, wired through .claude/skills/find-implicit-state/scripts/report.py, .pre-commit-config.yaml advisory dismissal-ledger-format hook. Dogfood: 5 real dismissals; semantic-edit resurface + cosmetic-edit stickiness both validated. Known v1 limitation (documented in scripts/_lib/ast_normalize.py header): superseded_by class-reference renames (e.g. Retailer→Site) cause AST hash change because v1 preserves module-level names; concepts.yaml-aware normalization deferred. Filter degrades to passthrough on missing/malformed ledger so failure modes are non-destructive.

hypothesis: setup_mode is the top-level branch in pnci-pricing — every downstream pipeline decision flows from it (automatic / partshare / custom each route to a different Celery task). Today it is a stringly-typed CharField with a hand-rolled four-way dispatcher; the trap of blanket-dispatching discover_sitemaps_task for partshare/custom sites (where it silently does the wrong thing) is captured in user-memory feedback_setup_mode_aware_discovery_dispatch.md but not in shared docs. Hypothesis: promoting SETUP_MODE_CHOICES to a Django TextChoices enum and introducing a SetupModeDispatcher class (one method per mode, with the routing tree explicit) eliminates the silent-wrong-task class entirely. The work is ADR-0017 (Staged Boundary Rearchitecting) trigger shape — multi-file refactor with a real ADR.
summary: Surfaced 2026-05-19 in pnci-pricing maintainability lean cut Track 3 (10-findings-and-dispositions.md finding #1). Evidence: Exp 05 candidate #1 + user memory feedback_setup_mode_aware_discovery_dispatch.md. Today's shape: setup_mode CharField on Site with three values (automatic / partshare / custom); dispatch is hand-rolled four-way in multiple call sites. Failure mode: dispatching discover_sitemaps_task for a partshare/custom site silently succeeds while doing the wrong thing (no crawler runs because there is no sitemap). Proposal: promote SETUP_MODE_CHOICES to TextChoices enum on Site; introduce SetupModeDispatcher with one method per mode and the routing tree explicit; replace every call-site that branches on setup_mode with a single dispatcher.invoke(action, site) call. Lint hardening: add a setup-mode-dispatch lint that blocks raw if site.setup_mode == 'automatic': branches outside SetupModeDispatcher. Revisit-when: next time we add a fourth or fifth setup-mode path, or feedback_setup_mode_aware_discovery_dispatch.md triggers a third burn.
title: Promote setup_mode to TextChoices + introduce SetupModeDispatcher

hypothesis: A single extraction field (e.g. part_number) has its spec scattered across 5+ structures in 3+ files: DEFAULT_FIELD_EXTRACTION_PROMPTS, FIELD_EXTRACTION_WORKED_EXAMPLES, _BASE_PROFILE_OVERRIDES, _FLATTENED_OVERRIDES, FIELD_VALUE_CONSTRAINTS, plus the DB row override on ExtractableField.extraction_prompt. This is the architectural-level analog of the _field_guidance failure mode (the case that motivated Track 2 of the lean cut); anyone editing one field's spec has to remember to update five other places, and the drift compounds with every new field. Hypothesis: a typed FieldSpec dataclass keyed by field name, with one canonical source per field that the runtime composes (prompt + examples + base profile + flattened override + value constraints + DB override), eliminates the scatter while keeping per-field override surfaces explicit.

title: Consolidate 5-dicts-in-3-files field-spec scatter into a typed FieldSpec

hypothesis: The site-intelligence-boundary lint draws a line but doesn't name what's outside it. Multiple adapters (_run_workflow_adapter, safe_dispatch, field-chat explicit-apply, do_not_apply_to_db_until_user_accepts) share a contract — artifacts in, decision outside — but no shared name. The 'WorkflowRunStatus=OK + outputs.decision=abstain' hidden-sub-status smell is the direct symptom: each adapter invents its own way to say 'don't apply'. Hypothesis: introducing SidecarWorkflowResult (typed result shape) + ApplyDecision (enum: apply / abstain / repair / human-review) + ApplyGate.evaluate(result) (canonical AND-chain) collapses the adapter-specific encodings into one contract. Lint hardening: extend site-intelligence-boundary to require any boundary-crossing return to be a SidecarWorkflowResult.
